author: ABMN Staff
title: Yellowstone Partners LLC Reduces Holdings in Apple (AAPL)
text:
Posted by ABMN Staff on Apr 23rd, 2018 // No Comments 
Yellowstone Partners LLC decreased its holdings in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 4.9% in the 4th quarter, according to its most recent 13F filing with the SEC. The fund owned 33,619 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 1,738 shares during the period. Apple makes up 3.2% of Yellowstone Partners LLC’s holdings, making the stock its 6th largest position. Yellowstone Partners LLC’s holdings in Apple were worth $5,689,000 as of its most recent SEC filing. 
Several other institutional investors have also modified their holdings of AAPL. FNY Managed Accounts LLC raised its position in shares of Apple by 852.4% during the 2nd quarter. FNY Managed Accounts LLC now owns 800 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $115,000 after acquiring an additional 716 shares during the last quarter. Private Vista LLC bought a new stake in shares of Apple in the 2nd quarter valued at $122,000. Oak Point Wealth Management bought a new stake in shares of Apple in the 4th quarter valued at $163,000. Interactive Financial Advisors bought a new stake in shares of Apple in the 4th quarter valued at $188,000. Finally, Reaves W H & Co. Inc. bought a new stake in shares of Apple in the 2nd quarter valued at $200,000. Institutional investors own 61.28% of the company’s stock. 
In other news, SVP Daniel J. Riccio sold 17,375 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Wednesday, April 4th. The shares were sold at an average price of $169.12, for a total transaction of $2,938,460.00. Following the transaction, the senior vice president now directly owns 66,191 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $11,194,221.92. The sale was disclosed in a legal filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which can be accessed through the SEC website . Also, insider Philip W. Schiller sold 69,491 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Tuesday, April 3rd. The stock was sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total transaction of $11,564,692.22. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Insiders have sold 125,988 shares of company stock worth $21,336,201 over the last ninety days. Insiders own 0.06% of the company’s stock. A number of analysts recently commented on the stock. Vetr cut shares of Apple from a “strong-buy” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $186.86 price objective for the company. in a research report on Monday, April 2nd. Nomura set a $175.00 price objective on shares of Apple and gave the company a “neutral” rating in a research report on Tuesday, April 3rd. BMO Capital Markets cut shares of Apple from an “outperform” rating to a “market perform” rating and upped their price objective for the company from $162.00 to $166.00 in a research report on Wednesday, January 31st. Royal Bank of Canada set a $203.00 price objective on shares of Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research report on Tuesday, April 3rd. Finally, Morningstar set a $170.00 price objective on shares of Apple and gave the company a “neutral” rating in a research report on Friday, February 2nd. Two equities research analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have issued a hold rating, thirty-two have issued a buy rating and one has assigned a strong buy rating to the company’s stock. Apple has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus target price of $203.15.
Apple stock opened at $165.72 on Monday. The stock has a market capitalization of $840,865.50, a price-to-earnings ratio of 17.03, a P/E/G ratio of 1.26 and a beta of 1.25. The company has a current ratio of 1.24, a quick ratio of 1.20 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74. Apple has a twelve month low of $141.85 and a twelve month high of $183.50. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its quarterly earnings results on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 earnings per share for the quarter, beating the Thomson Reuters’ consensus estimate of $3.82 by $0.07. Apple had a net margin of 21.13% and a return on equity of 37.37%. The firm had revenue of $88.29 billion for the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $87.62 billion. During the same period in the prior year, the firm earned $3.36 EPS. The business’s revenue was up 12.7% on a year-over-year basis. equities analysts forecast that Apple will post 11.3 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
